title: Minecraft
wiki_lead:
Minecraft is a sandbox video game developed and published by the Swedish company Mojang Studios. Following its initial public alpha release as an early access title on 17 May 2009, it was formally released on 18 November 2011 for personal computers. The game has since been ported to numerous platforms, including mobile devices and various video game consoles.
In Minecraft, players explore a procedurally generated world with virtually infinite terrain made up of three-dimensional blocks represented as voxels. They can discover and extract raw materials, craft tools and items, build structures, fight hostile mobs, and cooperate with or compete against other players in multiplayer. In addition, the game's large community offers a wide variety of user-generated content, such as modifications, servers, player skins, texture packs, and custom maps, which add new game mechanics and possibilities.
Originally created by Markus "Notch" Persson using the Java programming language, Jens "Jeb" Bergensten was handed control over the game's development following its full release. In November 2014, Mojang and the Minecraft intellectual property were purchased by Microsoft for US$2.5 billion; Xbox Game Studios holds the publishing rights for the Bedrock Edition, the unified cross-platform version which evolved from the Pocket Edition codebase and replaced the legacy console editions. Bedrock is updated concurrently with Mojang's original and PC-exclusive Java Edition, although with numerous, generally small, differences.
Minecraft is the best-selling video game of all time with over 400 million copies sold. It has received critical acclaim, winning several awards and being cited as one of the best video games ever made. Social media, parodies, adaptations, merchandise, and annual Minecon conventions have played prominent roles in popularizing it. A film adaptation, titled A Minecraft Movie, was released in 2025 and became the second highest-grossing video game film at the time of its release.

Gameplay
Minecraft is a three-dimensional (3D) sandbox video game played in discrete, persistent instances called "worlds". These worlds are composed of rough 3D objects—mainly cubes, referred to as blocks—arranged in a voxel grid and representing various materials, such as dirt, stone, ores, wood logs, water, and lava. The core gameplay revolves around picking up and placing these blocks: players can move freely around the world, breaking, or mining, blocks and then placing them elsewhere to build structures. Most blocks are not affected by gravity, instead maintaining their voxel position in the air. Minecraft has no required goals to accomplish, giving players a large amount of freedom in choosing how to play the game, though an optional achievement system is included. Gameplay is in the first-person perspective by default, but players have the option of third-person perspectives (back and front).
Players can craft a wide variety of items, including armor, which mitigates damage from attacks; weapons—such as swords or bows and arrows—which make it easier to kill monsters and animals; and tools—such as pickaxes or shovels—which break certain types of blocks more quickly. Some items have multiple tiers based on the material used to craft them, with higher-tier items being more effective and durable. Players may also craft functional blocks, such as furnaces, which cook food and smelt ores, and torches, which produce light. Additionally, players can trade with villagers (NPCs), exchanging emeralds for various goods. The game has an inventory system, allowing players to carry a limited number of items. The game's time system follows a day and night cycle, with one full cycle lasting 20 real-time minutes. The game also features a material called redstone, which can be used to build primitive mechanical devices, electrical circuits, and logic gates, enabling the construction of complex systems.

Players explore a procedurally generated, block-based 3D world, gathering resources to craft tools and items, build structures, and survive against hostile mobs and environmental hazards in survival mode, or create freely with unlimited resources in creative mode. In Survival mode, the primary way to complete or beat the game is by defeating the Ender Dragon in the End dimension, which triggers the end credits and signifies game completion. The game is available in Java Edition for personal computers and Bedrock Edition across consoles, mobile devices, Windows PCs, and other platforms. Bedrock Edition supports cross-platform multiplayer. There is no official full free version of Minecraft. A limited demo of Java Edition is available through the Minecraft Launcher, and Minecraft Classic, an early version of the game, can be played for free in the browser at classic.minecraft.net. Minecraft is distributed directly by Mojang Studios through the official Minecraft website and the Minecraft Launcher for Java Edition, and via the Microsoft Store and other platform-specific stores for Bedrock Edition. Purchases of Bedrock Edition are platform-specific and do not transfer; buying the game on the Google Play Store for Android does not grant access to play on a Windows PC, which requires a separate purchase from the Microsoft Store ($29.99 USD). Regional prices vary; in Turkey the Java & Bedrock Edition for PC was listed at âº1,199.00 as of March 2026, after roughly doubling from around âº509 in June 2025. Linking Microsoft accounts enables cross-platform multiplayer if the game is owned on both platforms. Notably, the core Minecraft game (both Java and Bedrock Editions) is not available for purchase or as a native title on Valve's Steam digital distribution platform as of March 2026. Minecraft spin-offs Minecraft Dungeons and Minecraft Legends are available on Steam. This decision stems from business considerations, including avoiding Steam's typical 30% revenue cut on sales, and retaining full control over in-game monetization features such as the Minecraft Marketplace (for add-ons, skins, and texture packs), cosmetic items like capes, and subscription services. Historically, in 2011, creator Markus Persson (Notch) explained that being on Steam would limit Mojang's ability to implement certain features and communicate directly with users in ways compatible with Valve's platform policies, potentially fragmenting the community. Users who own Minecraft can add the Minecraft Launcher (or executable) to their Steam library as a non-Steam game. This allows launching the game from Steam for convenience, access to the Steam overlay (in some configurations), and controller configurations, though it lacks full Steam features such as achievements, trading cards, cloud saves specific to Steam, or accurate playtime tracking for core gameplay. First publicly released in 2009, its full version launched in 2011. Microsoft acquired Mojang in 2014. Minecraft is widely regarded as the most popular video game and is the best-selling video game of all time, with over 425 million copies sold worldwide as of September 2026 and over 212 million monthly active users as of 2026. Its enduring popularity is attributed to its open-world sandbox gameplay that enables unlimited creativity and building, combined with survival and exploration elements, strong community engagement through mods and user-generated content, regular updates adding new features, cross-platform multiplayer support, and broad appeal across ages. It is widely regarded as a video game that defined childhood for many people, especially those in the 2010s and early 2020s, due to its emphasis on creativity, building, exploration, and limitless imagination. Commentators have identified it as one of the most important games of the 2010s and a defining element of that decade's gamer, YouTube, and internet culture.
